data.name: Threshold sensitivity analysis
data.research_question: How do precision, recall, false positives and contextual recall change across validation-derived thresholds?
data.hypothesis: Higher percentiles will reduce false positives at the cost of contextual recall, while original positive recall may remain high.
data.algorithm: Percentile sweep over benign validation reconstruction errors
data.training_strategy: Analytical study; no additional model training.
data.results_summary: For E2-D, P99 yields 70 TP / 8,628 FP and 77.33% contextual recall; P99.95 yields 70 TP / 2,339 FP and 49.33% contextual recall.
data.interpretation: Threshold choice strongly trades false-positive volume against contextual recall; P99 remains the primary experimental operating point.
data.limitations: P99.95 and related high-percentile points are retrospective diagnostics, not independently validated operating points.

warnings: Static aggregate snapshot. Event-level provenance is intentionally excluded.
